newsitem.title: USA: Russia official, rating agencies see Eurobond talk.
newsitem.headline: Russia official, rating agencies see Eurobond talk.

text.p: Russian Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov is likely to meet debt rating agencies in the coming days on Russia's plans for a debut Eurobond, international monetary sources said on Friday.
No details were immediately available on the timings of the talks, on the fringes of the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.
"I understand they will have meetings with rating agencies over this Eurobond issue and some other meetings with Western commercial banks," a monetary source said.
"That, I think, is the main reason for Kasyanov to come," the source added.
Russian officials have said Russia will make a first issue of $300-500 million of Eurobonds later this year. Russia has mandated JP Morgan and SBC Warburg to manage the issue.
A rating is seen as an important pre-requisite.

Three rating agencies visited Russia in September and Jochen Wermuth, head of the Russian finance ministry's Economic Experts Group, told a news conference in Moscow on Friday they would likely issue their ratings in November.
He said one of the agencies was from Europe and two were from the United States. Western bankers have said one of the agencies is Standard & Poors.

Russia's international capital markets debut has been brought closer by its $10 billion IMF loan, agreed earlier this year, and big progress on rescheduling Soviet-era debts with both the London and Paris clubs of creditors.
Germany's Deutsche Bank AG said on Friday that virtually all of the debt eligible to be included in a London Club rescheduling had been committed by creditors and that reconciliation was under way.
The bank made the statement after a meeting between Kasyanov and Deutsche official Christian Vontz, who chairs the London Club of commercial bank creditors.
Russia said this month that enough of the $35 billion debt had been committed for a global restructuring to go ahead.
A number of local authorities, including Moscow, are mulling Eurobonds. The Sverdlovsk region, around the Urals city of Yekaterinburg, said on Friday it planned an issue.

Kasyanov is part of a 150-strong Russian team, led by First Deputy Prime Minister in charge of the economy Vladimir Potanin and central bank chairman Sergei Dubinin, expected to attend the IMF/World Bank meetings. Finance Minister Alexander Livshits will also attend.

Russia's three-year loan under the IMF's Extended Fund Facility is subject to tough monthly monitoring. An IMF team was in Moscow last week but monetary sources have said no decision on disbursement of the latest tranche of about $330 million is expected until after the IMF/World Bank meetings.

Ahead of the main meetings, U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission Chairman Arthur Levitt met Dmitry Vasilyev, head of Russia's Federal Commission for the Securities Market on Thursday, an SEC spokesman said.
They discussed the U.S.-Russia Capital Markets Forum, set up earlier this year under a commission led by U.S. Vice President Al Gore and Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
